verres , is (collat. form of the
I.nom. sing. verris , Varr. R. R. 2, 4, 8), m. Sanscr. root varsh-, to rain, wet; whence vrshabha, bull; cf. ἔρση, dew, a male swine, boar-pig (syn.: “aper, porcus),” Varr. R. R. 2, 4, 21 ; Col. 7, 9, 7; Hor. C. 3, 22, 7.— Transf., contemptuously, of a man, Plaut. Mil. 4, 2, 67.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
